Can we meet at the library instead? Same time, half past four.

I have your book with me.

See you there,

Dan —

A parcel came for you this morning. It was too big for the box, so it is under my bed.

I am out until nine. Just knock, I do not mind how late.

The man asked me to sign. I hope that is all right.

Priya

items.stem: When can Dan collect it?

Dear parents,

Our trip to the farm is on Friday.

The bus leaves at nine. Please come at ten to nine, not later.

Children need a coat and a packed lunch. The farm is wet in places, so old shoes are best.

We are back by half past three.

Ms Owen

items.stem: Why does the letter mention old shoes?
options: Parts of the ground are wet
The walk to the farm is long
New shoes are not allowed there
The floor of the bus gets dirty
items.rationale: It gives the wet ground as the reason for old shoes.

items.stem: What must children bring?
items.rationale: The letter asks for a coat and a packed lunch.

items.stem: When does the trip end?
items.rationale: The letter closes by saying the class is back by half past three, which is when the trip ends.

script:
Dear Mr Hale,

I live at flat 6. The window in the back bedroom will not shut properly. It closes, but there is a gap at the top and the rain comes in when the wind is from that side.

I have put a towel on the floor for now. The wood under the window is already dark, so I do not want to leave it many weeks.

I am at home on Tuesday and Thursday mornings. Any other day, my neighbour in flat 5 has a key and is happy to let someone in.

Could you let me know a day? A message is fine; I do not need a telephone call.

Thank you,
Anna Reyes

items.stem: What is wrong with the window?
options: It is broken in the middle
It leaves a gap when shut
items.rationale: It closes, but a gap remains at the top and rain enters when the wind blows that way.

items.stem: Why does Anna say she cannot wait long?
items.rationale: She points to the wood below the window already darkening as the reason not to leave it for weeks.

items.stem: How can someone get in on a Friday?
options: Through the neighbour with a key
items.rationale: On days other than Tuesday and Thursday mornings, the neighbour in flat 5 can let someone in.

items.stem: How does Anna want to be answered?
items.rationale: She says a message is fine and that a telephone call is not needed.

script:
Hello Marta,

Thank you for the ladder. The gutter is completely clear now.

I planned to return it on Sunday. Unfortunately one of the feet came off while I was folding it. I have found the missing part and I believe it fits back on. I did not force it, because I might have damaged something else.

The repair shop on Mill Lane can examine it on Wednesday. The man expects it to be inexpensive. I will pay whatever it costs.

Do you need the ladder before Wednesday? Tell me and I will return it immediately, exactly as it is.

Ben

items.stem: Why has Ben not returned the ladder?
items.rationale: A foot came off while he was folding it, so he has kept it back rather than hand it over damaged.

items.stem: Why did Ben not mend it himself?
options: He had no tools at all
He could not find the part
He had no time on Sunday
items.rationale: He found the part and thinks it fits, but did not force it in case he damaged something else.

items.stem: Who is paying for the repair?
items.rationale: Ben states that he will pay whatever the repair costs, and names the shop and the day.

items.stem: What does Ben offer to do?
items.rationale: If Marta needs the ladder before Wednesday, he will bring it back immediately in its present state.

script:
Subject: Cover for the next three weeks

Hi everyone,

As most of you know, Farah is away from Monday for three weeks. Rather than ask one person to absorb it all, I have split the work.

The order sheet moves to Ken, who already does it on Fridays, so this is more of the same rather than something new. The supplier calls go to Dolores. Neither of you should be doing your own job and this on the same day; if that is what is happening, tell me on the day and not at the end of the week, when it is too late for me to do anything about it.

The part nobody has volunteered for is the Thursday stock count. I am not going to assign it. It is two hours and it is dull, and I would rather one of you chose it than resented it. If nobody offers by Wednesday I will do it myself, which is not a threat, simply what will happen.

Farah has left notes in the shared folder. They are good notes, but they assume you know why the Tuesday order is placed early, and only Ken does. Ken, could you add a line?

Thanks,
Marcus

items.stem: Why has Marcus divided the work?
options: To spread it over three people
Because Ken is away as well
To get the work finished faster
items.rationale: He says he chose not to ask a single person to absorb all of Farah's work, and split it instead.

items.stem: Why does he give Ken the order sheet?
options: Ken already does it on Fridays
items.rationale: Ken already handles it on Fridays, so it is more of the same rather than new work.

items.stem: What does Marcus ask people to do straight away?
options: Report a clash the same day
items.rationale: He wants to hear on the day, because at the end of the week it is too late for him to act.

items.stem: Why will he not assign the stock count?
options: He would rather someone chose it
He has already given it away
items.rationale: He says he would rather one of them chose it than resented it, and will take it himself if nobody offers.

items.stem: What is missing from Farah's notes?
options: Why the Tuesday order is early
The time of the stock count
The name of the shared folder
items.rationale: The notes assume the reader knows why the Tuesday order goes in early, and only Ken does.

script:
Dear Ms Achebe,

We are writing about the date your monthly payment leaves your account.

At present it is taken on the twenty-eighth. From October it will be taken on the fourth of the month instead. The amount does not change and neither does anything else about your account.

We are making the change because a payment on the twenty-eighth falls before many people are paid, and we would rather move the date than continue to see payments returned. If the fourth suits you less well than the twenty-eighth, write or telephone and we will set a different day; almost any date can be arranged, and doing so does not affect your record with us.

One payment will be short. The September payment goes out on the twenty-eighth as usual, and the next on the fourth of November, which leaves October without one. You do not owe anything for that month; the schedule simply moves.

You do not need to do anything if the new date suits you.

Yours sincerely,
Customer Accounts

items.stem: What is the letter mainly about?
options: A move in the payment day
items.rationale: Only the day the money leaves is changing; the amount and everything else stay as they are.

items.stem: Why is the company making the change?
options: Because customers complained about the amount
items.rationale: The old date falls before many people are paid, and the company would rather move it than keep seeing payments returned.

items.stem: What happens if the new date does not suit?
items.rationale: The letter invites the reader to get in touch and says almost any date can be arranged.

items.stem: What does the reader owe for October?
items.rationale: October has no payment because the schedule moves, and the letter says nothing is owed for it.

items.stem: What must the reader do if the new date is fine?
items.rationale: The last line says no action is needed if the new date suits.

script:
Subject: Pausing my membership

Dear Sir or Madam,

I joined in March and I have been coming twice a week since. I am writing because I have surgery on my shoulder in three weeks and have been told not to lift anything for two months afterwards.

I would rather pause than cancel. I have looked on your website and can find the cancellation page easily, but nothing about a pause, so I may be asking for something you do not offer. If that is the case, please say so plainly and I will cancel and rejoin later; I would prefer a clear no to a form that quietly becomes a cancellation.

If a pause is possible, I would like it to run from the first of next month for three months, which allows a few weeks after the two.

I should add that I do not need a letter from the hospital to be requested. I can send one, but the surgery is not yet booked to a day, so the letter would say less than this email does.

Thank you,
Joanna Petrov

items.stem: Why is Joanna writing?
options: To ask whether a pause is possible
items.rationale: She asks to pause rather than cancel and is not sure the club offers it.

items.stem: Why is she unsure it can be done?
options: The website mentions cancelling but not pausing
items.rationale: She found the cancellation page easily and nothing about pausing, so she may be asking for something not offered.

items.stem: What does she say she would prefer?
items.rationale: She says a plain no is better than a form that quietly turns into a cancellation.

items.stem: How long does she ask for?
items.rationale: She asks for three months from the first of next month, allowing a few weeks beyond the two she was told to rest.

items.stem: Why does she mention a hospital letter?
options: To ask the club to request one
To explain it would add little at present
To prove she is a member
items.rationale: The surgery has no date yet, so a letter would say less than her email does.

script:
Subject: Refund for the withdrawn evening course — fourth request

Dear Ms Lindqvist,

I am writing for the fourth time about the same matter, and I would like to set out plainly where it now stands, because I think the record matters more than my irritation.

On 3 June I paid £340 for an eight-week evening course. On 11 June the college withdrew the course, citing low numbers. That is entirely reasonable and I have never disputed it. The college's own terms say that a withdrawn course is refunded within twenty-eight days.

I wrote on 14 June and was told the refund had been raised. I wrote on 2 July and was told the same. I wrote on 24 July and was told that the finance system had changed and that a small number of payments had been affected. Each reply has been prompt and courteous, and none has produced any money.

What I would like now is different from what I asked for before. I no longer want an assurance that it has been raised; I have three of those. I would like either the money, or a date — a real one, from someone who can see the system — after which I can escalate with a clear conscience.

I should say that I am not seeking compensation and have no wish to make a formal complaint. I would rather this ended quietly. But eleven weeks against a twenty-eight-day term is a long way past the point where patience is a virtue, and if I have not heard by the fifteenth I will write to the ombudsman, not out of anger but because I will have run out of other things to do.

Yours sincerely,
Declan Moore

items.stem: What does the writer say he is not disputing?
options: The decision to withdraw the course
items.rationale: He calls the withdrawal for low numbers entirely reasonable and says he has never argued with it.

items.stem: How does he describe the replies he has had?
items.rationale: He notes that every reply has been prompt and courteous while producing no money.

items.stem: What is he asking for that he did not ask for before?
options: A date he can rely on
items.rationale: He says he no longer wants an assurance and would accept either the money or a real date from someone who can see the system.

items.stem: Why does he mention the twenty-eight-day term?
options: To show he paid on time
To measure how far past it the college is
To ask for it to be extended
items.rationale: He sets eleven weeks against the twenty-eight days to show the gap between the term and what has happened.

items.stem: How does he present the mention of the ombudsman?
options: As a threat made in anger
As what is left when nothing else remains
items.rationale: He says it would not be out of anger but because he will have run out of other things to do.

items.stem: What does the writer say about a formal complaint?
options: He does not wish to make one
He will make one on the fifteenth
He was advised to make one
items.rationale: He states that he is not seeking compensation and has no wish to complain formally, and would rather it ended quietly.

script:
Subject: Roof work, and the things you are about to ask

Dear residents,

Scaffolding goes up on the ninth and the roof work should take five weeks. Rather than send the short version and answer the same questions forty times, here is the long one.

Yes, there will be noise, and it will start at eight. The contract says half past seven and we have asked for eight; that is the only concession we managed and we did ask.

No, the scaffolding does not mean anyone can climb to your windows. It will be alarmed at night and the ground-floor ladders are removed each evening. This is the question we are asked most and it is a fair one, so please do not feel awkward raising it again.

The car park loses six spaces for the duration. We considered allocating the remaining spaces by need, and decided against it: every scheme we drew up required someone to judge whose need was greater, and we did not want to be that person or ask a neighbour to be. They will be first come, first served, which is unfair in a different and more obvious way.

The cost is met from the reserve fund. It does not affect the service charge this year. Whether it affects it next year depends on what the reserve is asked to cover after this, which nobody can honestly answer yet.

Finally, the part we would rather not write. The survey found more decay than expected above flats 7 to 11. If it turns out to run further, the five weeks becomes seven or eight. We will tell you the day we know, rather than at the end of a week when the news has aged.

The Management Committee

items.stem: Why has the committee written at length?
options: To avoid answering the same questions repeatedly
items.rationale: They say they would rather write the long version than answer the same questions forty times.

items.stem: What does the letter say about the start time?
options: It could not be moved at all
Eight is a concession they obtained
Work begins at half past seven
items.rationale: The contract allows half past seven and they negotiated eight, describing it as the only concession they managed.

items.stem: How is the parking to be handled?
items.rationale: They rejected allocation by need and chose first come, first served, calling it unfair in a more obvious way.

items.stem: Why did they reject allocating spaces by need?
options: It would have cost too much
Someone would have to judge between neighbours
items.rationale: Every scheme required someone to decide whose need was greater, and they did not want that role or to give it to a neighbour.

items.stem: What do they say about next year's service charge?
options: The reserve fund will be closed
items.rationale: They say it depends on what the reserve is asked to cover next, which nobody can answer honestly at this stage.

items.stem: What is their approach to bad news about the roof?
options: To confirm it before saying anything
To report it the day they know
To include it in the annual report
To raise it at a meeting
items.rationale: They promise to tell residents the day they know rather than at the end of a week when the news has aged.

script:
Subject: Reference for Tomás Villanueva

Dear Ms Odell,

Thank you for asking. Tomás worked in my team for two and a half years and left of his own accord in April.

He is careful. I do not use that word loosely. In a department where the cost of an error is measured in weeks, he made very few, and the ones he made he raised himself before anyone found them. He is also the only person I have managed who consistently read a brief to the end before starting.

You ask specifically about leading a team of six. I have to be straightforward with you: I do not know. Tomás led a project of three for four months and it went well, though I would say the three were unusually experienced and largely led themselves. He has not been tested by anyone who needed managing rather than informing, and I would not want to tell you he has when he has not.

What I can say is that when he did not know something, he said so on the day rather than at the review, which in my experience is the harder half of the job and the half people do not learn.

He was not the fastest member of the team and would not claim to be. If the role rewards speed above accuracy, there are people who would suit it better. If it is the other way round, I would take him back tomorrow, and I say that having been the person who accepted his resignation.

Yours sincerely,
Priya Raghunathan

items.stem: What is the writer's overall position?
options: A warm recommendation with a stated limit
A recommendation she was told to give
items.rationale: She praises him strongly and says she would take him back, while stating plainly what she cannot vouch for.

items.stem: Why does she mention the errors he made?
options: To show he reported them himself
items.rationale: The point is that the few errors he made he raised himself before anyone else found them.

items.stem: What is her answer about leading six people?
options: He is not capable of it
items.rationale: She says directly that she does not know, because the team he led was small and largely led itself.

items.stem: How does she describe the three he led?
items.rationale: She calls them unusually experienced and says they largely led themselves.

items.stem: What does she call the harder half of the job?
items.rationale: Admitting on the day rather than at the review is what she calls the harder half, and the half people do not learn.

items.stem: What kind of role does she suggest may not suit him?
options: One that rewards speed over accuracy
items.rationale: She was not the fastest, and she says others would suit a role that puts speed above accuracy.

items.stem: Why does she mention accepting his resignation?
options: To show she was glad he left
To give the offer its weight
To explain a gap in his record
To correct his account of leaving
items.rationale: Saying she would have him back while having been the one who accepted his resignation is what gives the offer its force.
